Client Libraries

Abbreviations used on this page (TSDB, WAL, TTL, HWM, XPUB, ZMQ, SQLite, JSON, CLI, API, RSS, fd, PEP, CORS, OBS...) are defined in the Abbreviations & jargon section.

sqtseries speaks JSON over two transports, so any language can talk to it without a special driver:

TransportBest forPorts
ZeroMQ (tcp://127.0.0.1) High-volume senders, live subscribers, admin 12501 ingest (PUSH), 12502 query (REQ), 12503 subscribe (SUB), 12504 admin (REQ), 12506 stats (SUB)
HTTP (http://127.0.0.1:12505) Anything with an HTTP client — curl, browsers, scripts 12505 (REST + WebSocket)

Both transports use the same JSON shapes. The one consistent difference: query start/end are epoch nanoseconds on the ZMQ path and epoch seconds on the HTTP path. Ingestion timestamps are seconds on both; query results are always seconds.

Python

The bundled sqtseries.Client wraps the ZMQ transports: write 12501, query 12502, subscribe 12503, admin 12504. Override with Client(host=..., ports={...}).

from sqtseries import Client

c = Client()  # defaults to 127.0.0.1, ports 12501-12504

c.write("cpu.usage", 0.72, {"host": "web1", "env": "prod"})
c.write_many([
    {"metric": "cpu.usage", "tags": {"host": "web1"}, "value": 0.72},
    {"metric": "mem.usage", "tags": {"host": "web1"}, "value": 512.0},
])

# query (start/end in NANOSECONDS; rows carry epoch-seconds timestamps)
import time
now_ns = time.time_ns()
rows = c.query("cpu.usage", start=now_ns - 3600 * 10**9, end=now_ns,
               aggregation="avg", interval="15m", limit=100, order="asc")
stat = c.aggregate("cpu.usage", funcs=["avg", "max", "p95"])   # {func: value}

# subscribe: yields dicts, or None as an idle heartbeat every ~0.5s
for payload in c.subscribe("cpu."):
    if payload is not None:
        print(payload)

# admin: ping | health | stats | connections | conncheck | subscribers
#        | optimize | backup | vacuum
c.admin("health")   # {"status":"ok","version":"0.1.0","uptime":N,"database":true}
c.admin("stats")    # counters and DB sizes; keys listed in the API reference

c.close()            # idempotent
# or: with Client() as c: ...

ClientError is raised when a query, aggregate, or admin command returns an error reply — and when no reply arrives within the client's 30-second receive timeout. close() is safe to call twice; the class is also a context manager.

The raw ZMQ call for a write, for anything that is not Python:

import zmq, orjson

ctx = zmq.Context()
sock = ctx.socket(zmq.PUSH)
sock.setsockopt(zmq.SNDHWM, 10000)
sock.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 500)
sock.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12501")
sock.send(orjson.dumps({"metric": "cpu.usage", "tags": {"host": "web1"}, "value": 0.72}))
sock.close(linger=0)
ctx.term()

Go

# go get github.com/pebbe/zmq4
package main

import (
    "encoding/json"
    "log"
    zmq "github.com/pebbe/zmq4"
)

func main() {
    // write (PUSH, fire-and-forget)
    sock, _ := zmq.NewSocket(zmq.PUSH)
    defer sock.Close()
    sock.SetLinger(500)
    sock.SetSndhwm(10000)
    sock.Connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12501")
    p := map[string]any{"metric": "cpu.usage", "tags": map[string]string{"host": "web1"}, "value": 0.72}
    data, _ := json.Marshal(p)
    sock.SendBytes(data, 0)

    // query (REQ) — start/end are NANOSECONDS; set a receive timeout
    qs, _ := zmq.NewSocket(zmq.REQ)
    defer qs.Close()
    qs.Connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12502")
    qs.SetRcvtimeo(30_000)
    req, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
        "type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage",
        "aggregation": "avg", "interval": "15m",
    })
    qs.SendBytes(req, 0)
    reply, _ := qs.RecvBytes(0)
    log.Println(string(reply))
}

Rust

# Cargo.toml: zmq = "0.10", serde_json = "1"
use serde_json::json;

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let ctx = zmq::Context::new();

    // write (PUSH, fire-and-forget)
    let sock = ctx.socket(zmq::PUSH)?;
    sock.set_linger(500)?;
    sock.set_sndhwm(10_000)?;
    sock.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12501")?;
    sock.send(json!({"metric": "cpu.usage", "tags": {"host": "web1"}, "value": 0.72}).to_string().as_bytes(), 0)?;

    // query (REQ) — start/end are NANOSECONDS
    let qs = ctx.socket(zmq::REQ)?;
    qs.set_rcvtimeo(30_000)?;
    qs.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12502")?;
    let req = json!({"type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage", "aggregation": "avg", "interval": "15m"});
    qs.send(req.to_string().as_bytes(), 0)?;
    let reply = qs.recv_bytes(0)?;
    println!("{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&reply));
    Ok(())
}

PHP

PHP has no widely available ZMQ extension — use the HTTP gateway. Timestamps here are epoch seconds:

<?php
// write
$ch = curl_init("http://127.0.0.1:12505/api/v1/write");
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POST, true);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS, json_encode([
    "metric" => "cpu.usage", "tags" => ["host" => "web1"], "value" => 0.72,
]));
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, ["Content-Type: application/json"]);
curl_setopt($ch, CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER, true);
echo curl_exec($ch);

// query (seconds on HTTP)
echo file_get_contents(
    "http://127.0.0.1:12505/api/v1/read?metric=cpu.usage&aggregation=avg&interval=15m"
);

Node.js

// write
await fetch("http://127.0.0.1:12505/api/v1/write", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ metric: "cpu.usage", tags: { host: "web1" }, value: 0.72 }),
});

// query (seconds on HTTP)
const r = await fetch(
  "http://127.0.0.1:12505/api/v1/read?metric=cpu.usage&aggregation=avg&interval=15m"
);
console.log(await r.json());

// subscribe — metric is a single topic prefix; pings arrive as {"type":"ping"}
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://127.0.0.1:12505/ws/subscribe?metric=cpu.");
ws.onmessage = (e) => {
  const msg = JSON.parse(e.data);
  if (msg.type !== "ping") console.log(msg);
};

Another Python service (separate venv / process)

sqtseries runs as its own process (for example under systemd). If your other Python project has its own virtualenv and does not want sqtseries installed, do not import it — talk to the running service over the wire, exactly like PHP or Node.js. Two options:

HTTP (zero dependencies, best for one-off calls and browsers):

import httpx  # or urllib, requests, aiohttp, ...

c = httpx.Client(base_url="http://127.0.0.1:12505")

# write (timestamp optional; epoch seconds)
c.post("/api/v1/write", json={"metric": "cpu.usage", "value": 0.72, "tags": {"host": "web1"}})

# read — start/end are epoch SECONDS on HTTP
import time
now = time.time()
rows = c.get("/api/v1/read", params={
    "metric": "cpu.usage", "start": now - 3600, "end": now,
    "aggregation": "avg", "interval": "15m",
}).json()["data"]

# whole-window stats
c.get("/api/v1/aggregate", params={"metric": "cpu.usage", "funcs": "avg,max,p95"}).json()

# health / stats (no admin socket over HTTP)
c.get("/api/v1/health").json()
c.get("/api/v1/stats").json()

ZeroMQ (high-throughput ingestion / live subscription / admin; needs a ZMQ binding such as pyzmq):

import zmq, orjson, time

ctx = zmq.Context()

# write (PUSH, fire-and-forget; timestamp epoch seconds, optional)
push = ctx.socket(zmq.PUSH)
push.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 500)
push.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12501")
push.send(orjson.dumps({"metric": "cpu.usage", "value": 0.72, "tags": {"host": "web1"}}))

# query (REQ; start/end are epoch NANOSECONDS)
now_ns = time.time_ns()
req = ctx.socket(zmq.REQ)
req.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, 30000)
req.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12502")
req.send(orjson.dumps({"type": "query", "metric": "cpu.usage",
                       "start": now_ns - 3600 * 10**9, "end": now_ns,
                       "aggregation": "avg", "interval": "15m"}))
reply = orjson.loads(req.recv())

# subscribe (SUB; topic = metric-name prefix)
sub = ctx.socket(zmq.SUB)
sub.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12503")
sub.setsockopt(zmq.SUBSCRIBE, b"cpu.")
topic, payload = sub.recv_multipart()

# admin (REQ; 12504) — send {"cmd": "health"} etc.
adm = ctx.socket(zmq.REQ)
adm.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, 30000)
adm.connect("tcp://127.0.0.1:12504")
adm.send(orjson.dumps({"cmd": "stats"}))
print(orjson.loads(adm.recv()))
Time units at a glance: ingestion timestamps are epoch seconds on both paths; query bounds are nanoseconds on ZMQ and seconds on HTTP; query results are always seconds.

Guidelines

  • Set a LINGER on ZMQ sockets (500 ms) so messages are not dropped when a socket closes.
  • Ingestion is fire-and-forget: one frame per measurement, no acknowledgement and no ZMQ-level batching. Send frames as fast as your sender can; the server drains them in bursts and commits one transaction per burst. There is no "batch until the server flushes" contract to reason about.
  • Set a receive timeout on REQ sockets (the bundled client uses 30s). The server also enforces its own budget, query.timeout_s (default 30s): a query that runs longer gets a QUERY_TIMEOUT error back — see Queries.
  • Omit ingestion timestamps to let the server stamp with its clock (avoids the clock-skew guard and keeps the rollup consistent).
  • Use HTTP for one-off scripts; ZMQ for sustained ingestion, live subscription, and admin.
